Analysis of Synthetic Methane Production from CO + H as an Alternative to Blending H With 2 2 2 NG – Technology Advance/Outcomes This subtask aims to answer the following research questions when comparing with the H /NG 2 blending pathways: 1. What are the cost and environmental implications of synthetic methane production from zero-carbon H and various CO sources vs. blending H into NG pipeline? 2 2 2 2. What are the scale and purity level of various CO sources, and the cost, energy, and 2 emissions associated with the capture and purification of CO for CH synthesis process? 2 4 3. What are the cost and energy/emissions associated with the transportation of CO to the 2 CH synthesis plant? 4 4. What are the cost and energy/emissions associated with the CH synthesis process? 4 5. What are the levelized delivered energy costs and GHG and CAP emissions of the CH 4 synthesis pathway compared to H /NG blending pathways? 2 6. Are there regional synergies associated with CO sources and H production pathways? 2 2 Analysis of Synthetic Methane Production from CO + H as an Alternative to Blending H With 2 2 2 NG – Subtasks Performed by ANL and NREL 1. Evaluate the cost, energy use, and emissions of capturing, purifying, and transporting CO from various sources: This subtask will evaluate the scale and regional availability of 2 CO from various sources, including nearly pure CO sources (e.g., ethanol, ammonia, and 2 2 NG processing plants), high-concentration CO sources (e.g., refinery steam methane 2 reforming plants, cement plants), and low-concentration CO sources (e.g., power plants). 2 This subtask will also evaluate the cost, energy use, and GHG emissions associated with capturing and purifying CO from these various sources, as well as the direct air capture of 2 CO . The cost of compressing and transporting H and CO to the CH synthesis plant will 2 2 2 4 also be evaluated. 2. Model CH synthesis process: In this subtask, ANL will develop a detailed Aspen Plus 4 model for evaluating the SNG production process from clean H and CO pathways. The 2 2 Aspen model will provide the GREET model with material and energy balance, carbon conversion ratio, and synthetic CH product yield. ANL will also use the model to size and 4 cost the major equipment needed for the SNG production needed by the TEA model. ANL will integrate NREL analysis on available clean energy sources for H production with 2 available sources of CO to estimate potential H demand by region for blending and for 2 2 SNG production. 3. TEA of SNG production: ANL will leverage the Hydrogen Analysis (H2A) modeling framework with TEA models using detailed capital and operation costs from the Aspen Plus process model, along with common economic and financial assumptions, to calculate the cash flows and levelized cost of the final SNG product.
